Preface

I'm still riled up from this daily issue despite a few journal entries to cool off, so I felt like writing a post here to ease the mind a bit more. This isn't Facebook, so I'm going to anonymize a few details that don't matter. To make a long story short, I am being set an improbable goal every day that I never meet. When I don't meet the goal in time (almost all the time), my managers get mad at me.

Background

I work in logistics and freight in a retail store. I break down pallets, stock the shelves, and help out customers. Usually, I am scheduled to do all this by myself most days without help. In addition to stocking shelves from the daily freight, I am assigned to do a fill report.

A fill report is a sheet of paper that tells me what needs to be stocked based on gathered data and some sort of algorithm. Just like my other freight duties, I am given a time limit, or what they call a 'goal', to complete the fill report. One minute per item.

How it goes down

So, the fill report is pretty much a pair of dice that decides how hard that day's going to be. Fill reports are supposed to be only 8-10 items long. That's on a good day. Unfortunately, most days, it climbs to more than 20 or 30 items long. The problem with longer fill reports is not that it takes longer to do them, but it takes exponentially longer to complete them the more items there are. I'll explain this later.

I'm going to explain the first, obvious problem. Having one minute per item. Two problems:

  • it's a static value given to a varying item
  • it's not even enough time

There are too many factors deciding how long I will inevitably take on each item. For any given item, it requires about 20 steps to cross it off the list. Each of these steps varies in time length and they range from moving my ladder to opening boxes to actually putting products on the shelves. I finally sat down today and actually calculated the actual time it would take me per item:

Minimum: 1 minute, 35 seconds
Maximum: 6 minutes, 8 seconds

So, the absolute max speed in ideal conditions still doesn't even make the goal. But, it doesn't even stop there. We need to factor in customers.

Customers take up anywhere from 30 seconds to (worst case) 20 minutes. On busy days, it gets horrible.

But, there's one last thing to factor in — the actual length of the task. Yes, that's right; the longer I take, the more of a factor that takes to make it even longer. How? Because customers. The longer it takes to complete the list, the more customers I'll eventually have to help.

So, on good days, It only takes about 30 minutes to complete a 10-item long fill report. But, on bad days, it can take up to 3 hours to complete a 25-item long report. Don't even get me started on the Record Breaker Fill Reports, which takes the cake with 47 items on a busy Saturday, taking five hours to complete.

In the end

But, hey, they have a right to get mad at me for not finishing, right? The fact is, I'm slower than a lot of logistics specialists because all of the others finish their tasks on time. Well, I wonder why?

Because they cheat!

Too bad I can't cheat. You can't exactly cheat logistically without getting bit in the butt later on. So, the fact that I care about the store is making the store hate me. Ah, well.

TL;DR: Give a man a spoon and a day to move a mountain, then get upset at him for not finishing weeks later.
